summary: 1. No new survey reading (`261010-INX-SUM.xlsx`) has landed for Oct 9 production, so [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] carries no update this pass. 2. Articles updated (Last updated 2026-10-10): daily-production-report, fleet-availability-utilization. 3. Key operational findings Oct 9 posted 12,400 BCM against a 12,036.1 BCM target (+3.0%), the second daily beat in a row, narrowing MTD to 302,715 BCM against a 324,974.9 BCM target (-6.85%, up from Oct 8's -7.2%) at the fiscal cycle's exact halfway point (day 15 of 30, 15 days remaining). 4. Three things to flag: 1. 5. The ore shortfall eased slightly (MTD -49.52%, from Oct 8's -51.6%) as today's mix ran far more ore-heavy than Oct 8 — stripping ratio fell to 4.41 from 18.1 — but MTD ore is still the second-deepest gap logged this cycle, and only one block (735-160-1/2, SHG) produced any ore today. 2. 6. The crusher logged its tenth consecutive zero-LCM stockpile-to-crusher day (Sep 30-Oct 9); MTD throughput sits at 9,753 LCM against a 62,000 LCM plan (15.73%, down from 16.85%) as the plan keeps growing on a running total unchanged since Sep 29 — this gap is now the widest it has been all cycle in percentage terms. 3. 7. The Drill Meters workbook's opening/closing Broken Stock and Drilling Stock figures tied out exactly against the Client Meeting Report for the first time with a clean before/after reconciliation (178,339 to 165,939 BCM broken stock, down exactly by today's 12,400 BCM production; 32,255 to 47,038 BCM drilling stock) — the cleanest tie-out of these two fields logged this cycle, resolving the standing reconciliation question from the Oct 7-8 passes. 8. Fleet availability: excavators 70.24% (MTD 65.51%), trucks 92.56% (MTD 91.59%), drill rigs 85.42% (MTD 86.92%), heavy vehicles 99.18% (MTD 99.19%), overall 88.14% (MTD 86.83%) — the strongest daily reading logged this cycle on every fleet shown. 9. EX-247 dropped off the down list entirely (zero stoppage entries, not even a daily inspection), a change from Oct 8's 10 h open engine-low-power breakdown; no explicit close time was found anywhere read this pass, so the fault's status is inferred, not confirmed. EX-253 and EX-263 remain down the full 24 h (day 24 and day 5 of their respective standing outages), together an estimated 17,654 BCM / 47,666 t at the day's four-running-unit average rate (367.8 BCM/h). DT-107 and DT-108 also logged a full 24 h down (day 16 and day 3), together about 3,008 BCM / 8,123 t at the fleet truck rate; two new truck faults opened overnight — DT-110 (front-right suspension, 4.5 h) and DT-129 (tyre air pressure leak, 6.5 h) — both still open at report time. Support Excavator, Wheel Loader, and Track Dozer did not extract as clean per-fleet summary blocks from this pass's Availability Report PDF (a change from the prior several days' extraction), and one drill-rig breakdown (hydraulic hose burst, night shift, 3.5 h) could not be matched to a specific unit ID — both flagged as open questions rather than guessed. A new light vehicle fault (LV-047, tyre flat, Breakdown-coded, 24 h) appeared that is not the previously-tracked LV-049 opportunity stop. The two new overnight voice notes (PTT-20261010-WA0011/0014) and the EX-247 handrail incident photos are registered but not transcribed or analyzed. `publish_insights.py` was deliberately not run this pass — the `wiki-insights-sync` task publishes separately. Source: KNOWLEDGE/mining_operations_kb/RAW via the librarian compile protocol.
